ei.title: The Dark Side of Being a Child Prodigy
ei.subject: 영어1

fullPassage:
The Dark Side of Being a Child Prodigy

We often read stories about extremely intelligent, gifted children. We might see an elementary school student who can play the most difficult classical music, a young boy who can do complicated math in his head, or a little girl who can get into a famous university before her 13th birthday. The surprising thing, though, is that these children aren't usually very successful as adults.

Some people might explain this by assuming that these extremely gifted young people have poor social skills or low emotional intelligence. In other words, these gifted children are too awkward, strange, and naive to succeed in the normal world. However, this theory is almost certainly wrong. Extremely gifted children usually have normal social skills and most of them are comfortable going to parties, talking with friends, and dealing with bosses or customers.

Instead, what seems to hold them back is their way of learning. All the time a gifted child spends memorizing Mozart is time he can't spend learning how to compose music himself. All the time an extremely intelligent child spends studying for university tests is time she can't spend learning how to think independently. In summary, these children tend to spend all of their time memorizing old ideas and skills but very little time coming up with new ideas or skills. This, unfortunately, is what most education encourages students to do.

According to many researchers, the skills that make someone a child prodigy simply aren't the same skills that make an adult genius. This is because the primary skill adult geniuses need is the ability to make new connections, create new ideas, and see new solutions to difficult problems. Unfortunately, child prodigies excel at doing the opposite — they become exceptionally good at doing problems that have already been solved, playing music that's already been written, and copying techniques that have already been developed. Practice makes perfect, but it doesn't make "new." Child prodigies who want to become adult geniuses, therefore, have to reinvent themselves before they can become innovators.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ successfully(부사) → 원문: successful(형용사). be동사 뒤 보어 자리이므로 형용사가 적절.
det.analysis:
① gifted: 형용사로 children 수식. 적법.
② complicated: 형용사로 math 수식. 적법.
③ successfully → successful: aren't usually very successful. be동사+보어=형용사. ←정답
④ assuming: by + V-ing 동명사. 적법.
det.tip: be동사 뒤 보어 자리에는 부사(successfully)가 아닌 형용사(successful)가 와야 한다.

The Dark Side of Being a Child Prodigy

We often read stories about extremely intelligent, gifted children.  We might see an elementary school student who can play the most difficult classical music, a young boy who can do complicated math in his head, or a little girl who can get into a famous university before her 13th birthday.  The surprising thing, though, is that these children aren't usually very successful as adults. 

Some people might explain this by assuming that these extremely gifted young people have poor social skills or low emotional intelligence.  In other words, these gifted children are too awkward, strange, and naive to succeed in the normal world.  However, this theory is almost certainly wrong.  Extremely gifted children usually have normal social skills and most of them are comfortable going to parties, talking with friends, and dealing with bosses or customers. 

Instead, what seems to hold them back is their way of learning.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 영재 아이들이 뒤처지는 근본적인 이유를 가리키는 표현을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (영어로, 4단어)

det.korean: their way of learning(그들의 배움 방식). 4단어.
det.analysis: 본문: what seems to hold them back is their way of learning. 이것이 영재 아이들이 뒤처지는 근본 이유.
det.tip: hold them back = 발목을 잡다. 그 원인 = their way of learning.

questions.passage: According to many researchers, the skills that make someone a child prodigy simply aren't the same skills that make an adult genius.  This is because the primary skill adult geniuses need is the ability to make new connections, create new ideas, and see new solutions to difficult problems.  Unfortunately, child prodigies excel at doing the opposite — they become exceptionally good at doing problems that have already been solved, playing music that's already been written, and copying techniques that have already been developed.  Practice makes perfect, but it doesn't make "new.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 연습이 만들어 내지 못하는 것은 무엇인지 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (영어로, 1단어)

det.korean: new(새로움). Practice makes perfect, but it doesn't make 'new.'
det.analysis: 본문: Practice makes perfect, but it doesn't make "new." 연습은 완벽을 만들지만 '새로움'은 만들지 못한다.
det.tip: new = 새로움. 연습이 만들 수 없는 것 = 새로운 것.

questions.passage:
However, this theory is almost certainly wrong.  Extremely gifted children usually have normal social skills and most of them are comfortable going to parties, talking with friends, and dealing with bosses or customers. 

Instead, what seems to hold them back is their way of learning.  All the time a gifted child spends memorizing Mozart is time he can't spend learning how to compose music himself.  All the time an extremely intelligent child spends studying for university tests is time she can't spend learning how to think independently.  In summary, these children tend to spend all of their time memorizing old ideas and skills but very little time coming up with new ideas or skills.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 영재 아이들의 발목을 잡는 것이 무엇인지를 가리키는 핵심단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (영어로, 1단어)

det.korean: learning(배움). what seems to hold them back is their way of learning.
det.analysis: 본문: Instead, what seems to hold them back is their way of learning. 발목을 잡는 것 = 배움의 방식. 핵심단어 = learning.
det.tip: learning = 배움. 사회성이 아닌 배움 방식이 문제라는 것이 핵심.

det.korean: ③ 신동의 학습 방식(암기 위주)이 성인 성공을 방해하는 이유.

det.tip: The Dark Side of Being a Child Prodigy = 신동의 어두운 면.

questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ 신동→성인 천재 전환을 위해 암기에서 벗어나 자기 재창조가 필요하다.
det.analysis:
① 본문과 반대: aren't usually very successful.
② 본문에서 부정됨: this theory is almost certainly wrong.
③ 글의 시사점이지만 직접 요지는 아님.
④ 글의 결론: reinvent themselves + 암기→창조 전환. ←정답
det.tip: 글의 결론: Practice makes perfect, but it doesn't make new. Reinvent themselves.

ch: 신동은 타고난 천재성 덕분에 성인이 되어서도 반드시 성공한다.
사회적 기술의 결핍이 영재 아이들의 성공을 가로막는 주요 요인이다.
교육 시스템은 학생들의 독립적 사고를 적극적으로 장려해야 한다.
신동이 성인 천재가 되려면 암기 중심 학습에서 벗어나 스스로를 재창조해야 한다.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 빈칸을 영어로 완성하시오.
"대부분의 교육은 학생들에게 이것을 하도록 __________." (이것 = 옛 아이디어를 암기하는 것)
[조건] (1) encourages, students, to, do를 모두 사용할 것 (2) 4단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: encourages students to do. 교육이 학생들에게 이것을 하도록 장려한다.
det.analysis: 본문: This, unfortunately, is what most education encourages students to do. encourage + 목적어 + to부정사 구문.
det.tip: encourage + O + to V: ~에게 ~하도록 장려하다. do = 옛 아이디어 암기.
